channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Samsung Reaches New Profit Record With Memory Chip Windfall
item.description: Samsung posted a record operating profit of about 107.4 trillion won, driven by demand for high-bandwidth memory. CLSA Korea Research Head Sanjeev Rana called the results broadly in line with expectations and noted he remains bullish on the memory cycle. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China’s Weak Holiday Spending Casts Shadow as Markets Reopen
item.description: Chinese shares will likely come under pressure upon their return from a week-long break, reflecting losses in the Hong Kong market and sluggish holiday spending.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu and Jiefei Liu

item.title: Malaysia Builds a New ‘Silicon Island’ to House Its AI Ambitions
item.description: Just south of Penang, the historic trading island off Malaysia’s northwest coast, excavators are turning a stretch of blue-green sea into a new, man-made island. Dump trucks crisscross freshly reclaimed sand as orange pipes snake across the emerging land mass, carrying fill pumped from dredgers offshore.
item.dc:creator: Netty Ismail

item.title: Ex-ByteDance Intern’s $200 Million AI Lab Takes On Fei-Fei Li
item.description: A former ByteDance Ltd. intern has secured funding from venture heavyweights including 5Y Capital for a stealth startup to take on AI pioneers such as Fei-Fei Li in the nascent realm of world models.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Samsung Reaches New Profit Record With Memory Chip Windfall
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. posted another record profit that was just shy of sky-high expectations elevated by surging memory chip prices and relentless spending on AI infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: SK Hynix’s Solidigm Is Said to Pick Banks for US IPO Next Year
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s Solidigm has picked lead banks for its US initial public offering next year, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz and Ian King

item.title: Broadcom Holds Early Talks About Financing for OpenAI Chips
item.description: Broadcom Inc., fresh off the launch of a $60 billion debt financing to help fund Anthropic PBC’s artificial intelligence build-out, is already sketching out plans for its next blockbuster deal.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass and Preeti Singh

item.title: US Agrees to Loan for Chipmaker That Went Bankrupt Last Year
item.description: The US Defense Department pledged to issue a conditional loan to Wolfspeed Inc., the chipmaker that filed for bankruptcy last year, for as much as $1.5 billion to support the development of materials that the firm described as key to national security.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Doan

item.title: Citi's Talent Fight with PE, Boots Deal, LIV's Lifeline
item.description: A weekly, midday program that delivers high-impact, editorially driven coverage of the most important corporate transactions shaping the global market. Today's guests: Permira Co-CEO, CO-Managing Partner Brian Ruder, Jefferies Senior Equity Research Analyst Shelia Kahyaoglu, McNally Capital Founder, Co-CEO & Managing Partner Ward McNally, 3wire Partners Founder & Managing Partner Anita Antenucci, and Citi Co-Head North Ameica Investment Banking David Friedland. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UPS Worker Missed Email, Letting China Get F-35 Parts
item.description: China managed to get a hold of parts from an F-35 stealth fighter jet after a United Parcel Service Inc. employee missed an email warning not to route the shipment through Hong Kong, according to a person briefed on the incident.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Musk Attacks Unnamed Indian ‘Oligarchs’ for Locking Out Starlink
item.description: Elon Musk accused unnamed rivals of blocking SpaceX’s Starlink satellite broadband network in India, an apparent swipe at billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Sunil Bharti Mittal.
item.dc:creator: Alisha Sachdev

item.title: Microsoft Says New Laptop With Nvidia Chip Outperforms MacBooks
item.description: Microsoft Corp. revealed pricing and availability for a new flagship laptop built on Nvidia Corp. chips, saying that the machine outperforms a comparable Apple Inc. model on some AI tasks.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Dazzle Wants to Turn Your Camera Roll Into an AI Assistant
item.description: Dazzle is betting the next generation of personal AI should know more about you before you even ask a question. The startup uses photos and screenshots in a user’s camera roll to understand their interests, relationships, travel and belongings — then helps take actions, from finding a product and arranging a repair to planning activities or adding an event to a calendar. Dazzle CEO Marissa Mayer joins Ed Ludlow for more on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sequoia, Nvidia Back Mecka AI’s Robotics Push
item.description: Mecka AI has raised $60 million in Series B funding led by Sequoia Capital, with backing from Nvidia, Microsoft’s M12 and Qualcomm, as it builds technology to help robots understand and operate in the physical world. CEO and cofounder Josh Gao discusses the enormous data challenge facing robotics, how Mecka captures everything from physical interactions to force and pressure, and why scaling physical AI will require major investments across sensors, infrastructure and real-world data collection. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rising Oil Puts Wall Street on Edge
item.description:
Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." SpaceX looks to raise $40 billion for Nvidia chips, Apple makes a bigger smart-home push with LG, and rising oil and rates cool Wall Street’s record rally. Plus, Apollo’s John Cortese on how the company is pushing to make private credit more transparent. New York Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli joins us on record banker bonuses and how the AI boom is impacting New York's bottom line and Alvarez & Marsal’s Paul Aversano on private credit, record profits and the M&A slowdown.
Correction: "This video was edited to correct the spelling of "Paul Aversano" that aired in the program at 10:10 am ET." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BofA Sees Strong Demand for OpenAI, Anthropic IPOs
item.description: Bank of America’s JD Moriarty says public markets have the capacity to absorb massive potential IPOs from companies including OpenAI and Anthropic, pointing to SpaceX’s listing as evidence of strong institutional and retail demand for transformational technology companies. He discusses how abundant private capital has changed the traditional IPO playbook and what the pipeline could mean for tech listings next year. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ring Founder Bets AI Will Transform Home Security
item.description: Ring founder Jamie Siminoff discusses the company’s expansion beyond its signature video doorbell into a broader smart-home security ecosystem, including its new smart lock. He weighs in on growing competition as Apple prepares to enter the category and explains why he sees cameras, locks and other connected devices becoming the physical “appendages” of increasingly powerful AI systems inside the home. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Partners With LG on New Smart Home Devices
item.description: Apple's upcoming push into smart home devices will include a doorbell, thermostat and other accessories developed through an unusual partnership with LG Electronics. The products will be part of an ecosystem that works with Apple's new smart home hub, according to sources. Bloomberg's consumer tech editor Mark Gurman joins Ed Ludlow with the details on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: William Blair’s Bitel Says AI Trade Keeps Market Narrow
item.description: William Blair Investment Management Chief Investment Strategist Olga Bitel says the market remains narrow, with investors focused on the biggest beneficiaries of the AI buildout. She spoke on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Falls as $550 Million in Risky Crypto Bets Wiped Out
item.description: Cryptocurrencies fell on Wednesday as a wave of forced selling swept across digital-asset venues, with broader market jitters further weighing on risk appetite.
item.dc:creator: Anna Irrera and Suvashree Ghosh
